title: DNF evaluation depends only on bounded variables
statement: Let $\psi$ be a DNF formula and let $a,b:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$ be assignments that agree at every index $v<N(\psi)$, where $N(\psi)$ is the variable count of the list of terms of $\psi$. Then $\psi$ has the same value under $a$ and $b$.
hypotheses_covered: $a,b$ are assignments from natural-number indices to Boolean values
the assignments agree for every $v$ strictly below the variable count of the terms of $\psi$
replaced:
Let $\psi$ be a DNF formula and let $a, b : \mathbb{N} \to \{0,1\}$ be assignments
with $a(v) = b(v)$ for every $v$ below the variable bound of $\psi$ (one more than its
largest variable index). Then $\psi$ evaluates to the same truth value under $a$ and
under $b$.
